title: Ferdinand I to Giovanni Battista Castaldo, Oct 1552 (catalogue 1332): all four letters read

steps.what: ff. 9r-15v and 34r-48v of G 275 inf. fetched from the Ambrosiana IIIF service, one request at a time.
Ledger, Carpentieri 2012 and two web searches; Dudout notes in research/dudout_2026-10-29/ read. Veress not opened yet.
Cipher lines of ff. 9r-10r and 34r-35v cut into shapes, clustered with no language, named by eye, labelled by a nearest-neighbour classifier (pass A).
Pass A of ff. 9r-9v aligned with the gloss of 9r-9v by EM. As run, 14 sign values were fixed in every restart and seven nulls were set by hand afterwards. Frozen as key_frozen.tsv.
Held-out f. 10r: frozen table on raw machine labels against the gloss, 442 of 518 letters in order (85.3%); shuffled tables best 41.5%.
Pass B: ff. 34r-35v read by eye on strips, not blind.
Decrypted and read; Hh, ii and 7 changed after the freeze with reasons in key.tsv.

Independent blind check (VERIFY.md): f. 34r, 350 signs, 6 differences (1.7%), 0 after zoom; own table from random starts gave 303 of 334 letters of its blind 34r. Found one phantom sign and a misdescribed method.
Corrections applied on the images: phantom sign at 35r.11 removed; doubtful signs marked at 34v.06, 35r.24, 35r.27. One disagreement with the check logged: the numeral at 34v.06 is nearer 8 than 5.
EM rerun with no seed values: locked at restart 21, all 36 frozen letter values the same.
Q7: margins, top and foot bands of 29 glossed pages read by eye; rho signs sought by a shape filter (11 found, none with a 7).
Veress, Documente I (1929), opened: no letter of 15 Oct; Nos. 135 and 137 print excerpts of the 18 and 22 Oct letters.

Full-texts audit: the machine labels of the 13 Oct letter already in pass_A_machine.txt (foot of f. 9r, f. 9v, f. 10r; 57 lines) copied to transcription_13oct_ff9r-10r_machine.txt and decoded with key.tsv (decryption_13oct_ff9r-10r.txt); listed with the marginal gloss as decoded, not read. The letters of 18 and 22 Oct (ff. 37r-42v, 43r-48v) and ff. 10v-15v have no transcription in the folder and none was made in this pass.

Sister letters of 13, 18 and 22 Oct (ff. 9r-14v, 37r-42r, 43r-47r): 35 pages segmented (scripts/seg3.py); a nearest-neighbour classifier trained on the 15 Oct eye transcription paired with the new segmentation (train_iter.py, 92% cross-validated); cipher lines marked by eye on annotated pages (cipher_lines.tsv, 528 lines, about 11,700 signs).

Language-model beam (la-letters 5-gram) choosing among the classifier top four labels per sign with key.tsv fixed; self-training on lines that scored well as Latin. Decode already Latin and in step with the margin gloss (e.g. f. 44v: habet enim pauciorem eorum numerum quam necesse sit).
A forced alignment of the reading to the classifier look-alikes was tried to cut the eye work; dropped because it chose confusing labels (drops and swaps not borne out by the image).

Eye pass: every line whose decryption differed from the reading checked on strips at 1.5x and corrected (eye_13oct.tsv, eye_18oct.tsv, eye_22oct.tsv), most lines typed whole by eye. Words exact rose from 75%, 73% and 59% to 98.7%, 98.9% and 95.4%.

Key extended: nulls Nx and Mx (N and M with long tail), numerals 4 dd and 12 tt (completing the series c3 d4 f5 g6 l7 m8 p9 r10 s11 t12), codes H6 the Moldavian voivode (gloss f. 38v foot "Modernus Moldauus", f. 39r "uayuoda") and Q1 princeps Turcarum (gloss f. 41v). No rho 7 occurs in the sister letters, so Q7 stays open.

Readings checked against the contemporary margin glosses page by page; where they differ the cipher is followed (e.g. "in dubitationem deducti", "regnique illius nostri", "presto futuros"), and spellings are the cipher's (catapractis, isthuc, opereprecium).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 5441 tokens, 61 types, la-letters order 4: reading -2.023 per letter; random keys -5.817 (z 8.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.531 (mean -3.561, z 52.9); annealer on the real text -2.023. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.02; polyphony 0.0; 27 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.023

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Table built by aligning machine labels of ff. 9r-9v with the contemporary gloss of the same pages, then frozen and tested on held-out f. 10r. The sister letters are the adjacent plaintext; the 15 Oct letter has no decipherment of its own.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Words in the cipher passages of the four letters that come out of the key letter for letter: 13 Oct 526 of 533, 15 Oct 311 of 317, 18 Oct 732 of 740, 22 Oct 584 of 612 (scripts/check_reading.py; NOTES table); 2153 of 2202. All but one word (code Q7) read as sense.

texts.label: 13 Oct 1552, f. 9r foot to f. 14v
texts.summary: Ferdinand is troubled by the mutiny of two companies of German foot and the doubtful loyalty of the Transylvanian estates, praises Castaldo for raising 20,000 florins for the heavy horse, sends money and cloth by Captain Stephen, explains that Maurice of Saxony is camped at Gyor to draw the Turks off Eger, and tells Castaldo to oppose the enemy without risking a grave defeat.
texts.note: Words 533 in the cipher passages; 526 come out of the key letter for letter (98.7%), the rest are the writer's slips or dropped letters at line ends (check_reading.py). Line-by-line reading: reading_13oct.txt.

reading_review.note: Read as running Latin against the margin gloss of the time; every cipher passage builds sentences, with codes rendered from key.tsv. Not reviewed by a second reader.

texts.label: 15 Oct 1552, ff. 34r-36r
texts.summary: Ferdinand would have liked a demonstration towards Lippa to draw the Ottoman army off Eger and to support Maurice of Saxony. He sends money and cloth, tells Castaldo to hold soldiers and subjects to their duty, and expects the enemy to be drawn off or driven off by winter.
texts.note: Words 317: 316 read as sense, 311 with no restored or changed letter, 306 with every doubtful sign out as well. One code word, Q7, is open.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. The cipher section reads as eight complete, grammatical Latin sentences with a clear argument: a wished-for feint towards Lippa to draw the Turks off Eger, money and cloth for the soldiers, and an order to hold soldiers and subjects to their duty until winter drives the enemy off. The decryption matches the reading letter for letter apart from four marked slips or missing letters (habemes, singslari, rationibu, diutiu), and the English follows the Latin faithfully. The real holes are few: code word Q7 is filled from context only (shown as ?Themeswar), the second Lippa rests on a doubtful numeral, a handful of single letters stand on blotted or faint signs, and the code values (Lippa, exercitus, Hamet, Transylvania) come from the sister letters' glosses rather than from a decipherment of this letter.

texts.label: 18 Oct 1552, ff. 37r-42r
texts.summary: The cavalry of Fabian von Schonaich wants to leave; money and cloth are on the way and the Reich common penny voted under the Treaty of Passau is coming in. Ferdinand asks for a feint towards Lippa to help Eger, reports plague in the Turkish camp, forbids Castaldo to leave Transylvania, and sets the terms for any peace: the tribute may be paid in Ferdinand's name or that of the three nations, but loyalty must be kept.
texts.note: Words 740 in the cipher passages; 732 come out of the key letter for letter (98.9%), the rest are the writer's slips or dropped letters at line ends (check_reading.py). Line-by-line reading: reading_18oct.txt.

reading_review.note: Read as running Latin against the margin gloss of the time; every cipher passage builds sentences, with codes rendered from key.tsv. Not reviewed by a second reader.

texts.label: 22 Oct 1552, ff. 43r-47r
texts.summary: Maurice cannot march to Eger: he lacks light horse and a defeat would shake Hungary, so he raids towards Veszprem and Szekesfehervar instead; Eger holds and winter is coming. Castaldo must stay in Transylvania to hold the passes of Deva against the Turks at Lippa, since Hamet stays with the army at Eger.
texts.note: Words 612 in the cipher passages; 584 come out of the key letter for letter (95.4%), the rest are the writer's slips or dropped letters at line ends (check_reading.py). Line-by-line reading: reading_22oct.txt.

reading_review.note: Read as running Latin against the margin gloss of the time; every cipher passage builds sentences, with codes rendered from key.tsv. Not reviewed by a second reader.

gaps.detail: Once in the 15 Oct letter; no rho 7 in the three sister letters (about 11,700 signs transcribed); [?Themeswar] from context only.
8 is kept and marked doubtful; Q5 cannot be excluded on the image.

gaps.item: Doubtful signs at 35r.24, 35r.27, 34v.05, 35r.18 and a few in the sister letters
gaps.detail: Faint, blotted, overwritten or interlinear; marked x? in the transcriptions.

gaps.item: Writer's slips in the sister letters
gaps.detail: About 40 words where the cipher itself drops or changes a letter (casis, inodedientes, nu-rum); read from sense and counted as not from the key.

prior.where: research/dudout_2026-10-29/ in this repository records that Brice Dudout read the 15 Oct letter (targets/castaldo1552, prepared locally), then withdrew it (validation 0.731 of words); held until he confirms. His files were not seen. Veress, Documente I (1929), Nos. 135 and 137 print excerpts of the 18 and 22 Oct letters; the 15 Oct letter is not there. Other editions and the Vienna minute were not checked (3 Nov 2026).

human: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1332) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, built the key, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
